thread:
sam: Heads up — onboarding sample app `generator-stream-demo` is brittle. If the SDK refreshes auth mid-stream the generator just stalls and we get no error back to the app. Repro steps + logs below.

sam: repro: start a long generator stream, force token rotation (short-lived creds), SDK does silent retry and the app waits forever. Log shows `stream: read EOF` followed by nothing.

sam: example snippet we used:
```go
ctx := context.Background()
c, _ := redwood.NewClient("$KEY")
stream, _ := c.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
for chunk := range stream.Chunks() {
    fmt.Print(chunk.Text)
}
// never hits error handler when auth rotate happens mid-stream
```

sam: filing because this blocks the sample app for new users and is a pretty bad first impression.

tian: thanks for the report. this sounds like a handshake/auth race where the runtime retries under the hood but we swallow the short-lived token error in the stream goroutine. can you paste the exact client version?

sam: using v0.7.1 (go module).

auth-bot: token-rotation-event: user/service-account rotate at 2026-02-28T14:12:03Z (forced test)

alla: I hit similar a while ago but it manifested as a silent stall only when the app didn't call `.Close()` on the stream. two things to check: 1) are you using a context with deadline, 2) do you have the stream error consumer running in a separate goroutine? 

sam: got a repro that includes context deadline, still stalls. error goroutine isn't getting a value.

kevin: quick idea — surface a `StreamState` event for mid-stream auth/reconnect attempts. SDK can emit something like `STREAM_WARNING: auth_refresh` so apps can log or decide to cancel. right now retries are internal and opaque.

tian: agree with kevin. we should not change automatic retry behavior yet (it helps reliability) but add observability and a deterministic final error when reconnects fail. also the Go generator API ergonomics could add a `Done() <-chan error` or `Err() error` accessor — that would make onboarding sample apps simpler.

jules: from a product/onsite docs perspective, the sample app should show best-practices: ctx with timeout, listen for `Err()` and expose a simple retry UX. if we add `STREAM_WARNING` events we can show them in Console too. this will reduce onboarding friction.

alla: here's a minimal change to the sample app loop that made it obvious in our internal test (pseudo):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute)
defer cancel()
stream, err := c.GeneratorStream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
// read loop
go func() {
    for ch := range stream.Chunks() { fmt.Print(ch.Text) }
}()
if err := stream.Wait(); err != nil { log.Printf("stream ended with: %v", err) }
```

alla: `Wait()` is our proposed alias for `Done()`/`Err()` — returns final error if any.

sam: that would be perfect. can we also make the SDK write a small log line when it internally retries auth so it's not invisible? even a `Debug` log would help.

tian: yeah — plan: (1) add `Wait() error` to GeneratorStream in next minor, (2) emit `stream.event: auth_refresh_attempt` to SDK logger, (3) add Console telemetry hook so we can show that event in the UI. I'll open a tracking issue.

kevin: also add a tiny example in `generator-stream-demo` showing how to surface and display that message (and a suggestion to cancel the stream if you want to abort on any retry).

jules: i'll update onboarding docs + quickstart text once the PR lands. wording: "If you see an auth refresh event mid-stream, your client may resume automatically; call stream.Wait() to observe final status and handle UX accordingly."

sam: thanks — assigning followups: tian will own SDK change, kevin will update sample app, jules will handle docs. i'll add a short snippet to the bug report so QA can rerun.

tian: filed issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/412 (stream-auth-retry-observability). will send a WIP PR with tests.

sam: excellent. marking this thread resolved for now. :thumbsup:
